A1.justification: Both readable 10-page PDFs describe MonoMobility and contain corresponding sections, equations, figures and tables. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; the supplementary material mentioned in both is not included.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative comparisons and ablations in Tables 1–3, alongside qualitative evaluations on synthetic and real-world scenes.

after.justification: v2 retains the original quantitative comparisons, ablation results and qualitative scene evaluations.

M1.justification: The preprocessing, Gaussian representation, initialization, optimization and losses are retained. The isolated symbol inconsistency introduced in Equation 4 does not establish an actual procedural change; its mathematical effect is assessed under T1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 15 simulated and 11 real-world scenarios, covering translation, rotation and combined motion. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain PARIS-scene, PARIS-obj and DGMarbles*, with the same adaptations and participation in Table 1 and Figure 4. The evaluated ablation variants also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The metrics, baseline input arrangements and evaluation procedures are unchanged. Section 5.4 retains 7,500 optimization iterations, classification at iteration 2,000, and the same initialization thresholds and loss weights.

E4.justification: Section 5.6 retains the same tests of axis initialization, individual loss removal and disabling optimization. Tables 1–3 and Figures 5–6 provide the same ablation evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and means without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and qualitative findings are retained. For example, Table 1 reports the same mean AE of 1.262 degrees and PE of 4.843 cm for the full method.

T1.justification: Equation 4 replaces the rotational-movement tests using φ^k and φ_min with t^k and t_min. The surrounding definitions still identify φ^k as rotational movement and t^k as motion type, while Section 5.4 still specifies φ_min. This introduces a local inconsistency in the formal classification rule, rather than an equivalent notation change.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about zero-shot monocular mobility analysis, self-supervised scene optimization and the constructed synthetic/real-world dataset.

C2.justification: The explanations of the optimization and loss functions are unchanged. Both versions retain the limitations concerning scene-specific optimization cost and dependence on depth and optical-flow estimates, including failures in highly dynamic scenes.

D1.justification: The preprocessing instructions, baseline adaptations, initialization details and hyperparameter disclosures are retained. No implementation, hardware, runtime or code/data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Artiscene and GRASS as references [8] and [20], included in the introductory citation range. The remaining works are retained under renumbering, and the related-work discussion and contribution positioning are otherwise unchanged.

P1.justification: Figure 2's final caption sentence is rewritten more concisely. Apart from citation renumbering and the version/date stamp, the prose and section organization remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 has a revised caption, and the added references cause bibliography reflow. The six figures and three tables retain their graphics, organization and placement; there is no substantial layout redesign.

improvement.justification: The clearer Figure 2 caption offers a small editorial benefit, and two references are added. However, Equation 4 introduces inconsistent t^k/t_min tests where v1 used the defined rotational quantities φ^k/φ_min. This creates avoidable ambiguity in motion classification. The limited loss of mathematical clarity outweighs the modest editorial changes, while the empirical evidence remains unchanged.
